key_distinction: REGISTRATION, not rendering medium. Every number here is about where a printed river (solid black line, by the cartographic key) sits relative to a city's cityBox footprint and approach circle. Plans are placed by cityBox around the anchor, and genCityCanvas draws a river only from traits.river (seeded bearing). A vector plan placed through the same cityBox with the same RV block would miss the printed river in exactly the same way. Only atlas-frame river geometry fed into the plan (registration) closes the gap; vector rendering only makes the mismatch crisper.
question: For every generated anchor: does a printed river stroke cross the 1.0*FOOT_R box and the 2.5*FOOT_R approach circle, and at which bearings? For Kolens and Ion Ephel, what can genCityCanvas's RV block draw? Which planned item would supply river polylines, and is its done-when precise enough to drive plan rivers? Is a fix hash-changing?

method.mosaic: maps-site/tiles/5 (35x18 tiles) pasted into an 8960x4608 RGB array, PIL JPEG decode (not the browser's); atlas px = z5 px / 2, no y flip. Throwaway numpy/scipy scripts in a mktemp -d dir; no browser.
method.dots: the dot detector behind out/vector-overlays-vs-print.json: 8-connected ink components with bbox 4-11 z5 px, fill > 0.55, aspect <= 1.6, chained to another dot within 16 z5 px; 2,514 candidates, 2,351 chained (the same 2,351 that file reports); dilated 2 px and removed.
method.coast: union of two coast bands, each = ink within 9 z5 px (4.5 atlas px) of both water and land. (a) the numpy buildCityMask port behind out/three-coasts-epeshu.json (lum >= 110 and r-b <= 54, separable radius-2 box blur, ratio >= 0.5), applied sheet-wide with water components >= 2000 z5 px kept. (b) DEVIATION, added because (a) alone fails under realm tints: a colour-distance sea mask (non-ink colour, 9x9 mean, within L2 9 of the sea tone RGB 175,167,128; opened; components >= 20000 z5 px; closed). Evidence: under the Pheropic/Eastern Patrin tint the land samples RGB 165,153,127 (r-b 36) and Emphēros land 154,152,106 (r-b 38), both under the r-b <= 54 water test, so (a) reads the tinted land as water and kept every Garnatos/Pheropic coastline (Graes, Sember, Kezren, Azrīnet, Gārmīt, Pel, Darā, Malau, Nīs Garnata...) as a 'river'. With (a)|(b) those all drop out.
method.lettering: text-component mask in the spirit of POLISH 'Traced road network' ('mask text components first'): letter cores = connected regions of distance-transform >= 2.6 z5 px with core area >= 20, core max DT >= 3.5 and bbox <= 60 z5 px (bold label stems; river cores measured <= 16 px area, the thick Tungril core is long, so neither is masked); cores dilated by 6 px and removed. Then any remaining component shorter than a 60 z5 px bbox diagonal (30 atlas px) is dropped: italic and small letters, ring-dots, dot remnants.
method.graticule: local Hough over ink minus dots in a 440x440 z5 px window per anchor: a line with >= 85% support along a chord >= 300 z5 px is a graticule line; ink within 2.5 px of it is removed. (A shorter chord first removed the straight Iet Ford river; 300 px fixed it.)
method.tests: box = square +-FOOT_R atlas px (capital 26, town 14, village 9, ruin 8) centred on the city-anchors.json anchor; ink_px_z5 = river pixels inside it; perimeter_bearings = runs of river ink (1 px dilation) along the box edge. Circle = radius 2.5*FOOT_R sampled every 0.25 deg; runs of river ink give crossing bearings, runs of the same component under 6 deg apart merged. Bearings are compass degrees from the anchor to the crossing point (0 = atlas up/N, clockwise; atlas y is top-origin). printed_axis_in_circle = principal axis (PCA) of river ink inside the circle, mod 180. within_wash_1_7x = nearest river ink <= 1.7*FOOT_R, the half-size of the washMake overlay bounds (washMake: var box=cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h),f=1.7).
method.adjudication: Every automatic flag was checked by eye on a montage (red = river candidate, blue = dropped ink, cyan = coast band, green = road dots, box and circle drawn) and, where unsure, on a raw context crop; verdicts and per-row notes record the outcome. A no-coast variant (coast band off) was run for recall: 86 extra anchors flagged, nearly all coasts; the 7 whose crossing point lay outside the coast band and 11 more were reviewed by eye; it recovered Heron's House (and gives the cleaner trace for Sau Taran). Rows marked variant 'nocoast' come from that run.
method.limits: Rivers cut by labels or by the coast band near a mouth may be missed or shortened (mouths inside 4.5 px of the coast always are). Lake shores (Five Fingers) are not separable from rivers by colour and were rejected by eye. Not every one of the 86 no-coast extras was viewed; the outside-the-coast-band filter is the recall screen. PIL decode, not browser decode.

summary.summarch: Summarch (the other canon DM chart) has no city-anchors.json entry, so it has no cityBox, no row here and was not tested.
summary.generated_with_traits_river: 1 of the 18 (Ion Ephel). Kolens, the other traits.river city, has no printed river within 2.5*FOOT_R.
summary.canon: Epēshu (DM chart, capital): the Lamor river crosses its 2.5*FOOT_R circle at 178.1 deg; its nearest ink is 37.7 px away, outside the 26 px box but inside the 44.2 px wash bounds.
summary.all_18_plus_epeshu_within_wash: Every one of the 19 printed rivers comes within 1.7*FOOT_R of its anchor, so each runs into the washMake overlay (alpha per shift_sources wash-ring-over-sea: 50-94% between the plan vignette and the wash fade-out) as well as the plan.

counts_by_kind.note: box_yes = river ink inside the 1.0*FOOT_R box; box_graze = 4-5 z5 px only (Bash Dargis, Ion Ephel); approach_only = river crosses only the 2.5*FOOT_R circle (Drāmūz, Aldrakhar town; Iet Ford village, whose river touches the box edge within the 1 px dilation). By kind: villages 13 of 115 (11%), towns 4 of 17 (24%), ruins 1 of 3, the capital (canon art) 1 of 1.

kolens_ion_ephel.rv_block: genCityCanvas: var rvFa=(rvBeside&&sv)?Math.atan2(sv.y,sv.x)+rr(-.35,.35):R()*Math.PI*2; // beside a coast: flow meets the sea. Through: any bearing, uniform. Beside: the sea vector sv +-0.35 rad (+-20.1 deg). The river axis is rvAx=(cos rvFa, sin rvFa) on a canvas mapped to the atlas without rotation (scl=S/(2*footR(a.kind))), so compass axis = rvFa in degrees + 90. The RV draw sequence was replayed in node with xmur3/mulberry32 taken from the HEAD source: draws before the RV block are only pick(Object.keys(COMPASS)) for a harbor with no sea.side and the 12 lobe draws.

living_trace.item: POLISH 'Living later · trace the rivers (data, tool)'
living_trace.frame: stated: 'every polyline has >= 8 vertices in top-origin atlas px', the same frame as city-anchors.json atlasX/atlasY, so a plan can take it through its existing linear map (canvas = (atlas - anchor)*S/(2*FOOT_R) + S/2) with no new transform.
living_trace.scope: sheet-wide; the only planned source for the 13 river cities outside the window.
living_trace.consumer: 'It feeds only "Living later · river flow and barges"' and its done-when requires '`maps-site/index.html` sha unchanged', so wiring polylines into genCityCanvas is new work that no item holds.
living_trace.blocked_by: 'Traced road network' checked; Filigree 4 passed; Mobile 9 and Mobile 14 checked.

why_not: Byte-identical twin runs settle determinism only; they say nothing about where a river lies.

'within 3 px of Filigree's rivers.json over >= 90% of its length' checks against another trace, not the print, and only inside the window. For the 13 out-of-window river cities nothing checks geometry against the ink at all; the remaining gates (canon names within 40 px, <= 20% within 6 px of a traced road, no vertex in F08) do not test position.

3 atlas px is 1/6 of a village box (2*9 px), about 341 canvas px of a 2048 village plan, which is about 341 screen px at a village's cityMaxZ 10.83 (where 1 plan px is about 1 screen px). And the 10% of length left unconstrained can be exactly the stretch inside a footprint.
No recall gate: nothing requires each printed reach to be traced, so a river at a town can be missing and still pass.

The text-component mask it reuses cuts rivers exactly where town labels sit on them (Ion Ephel, Aldrakhar 'Al', Lokri, Drāmūz 'z'; q10 had to bridge P1 under the L of LEPONIA by hand, 36.5 px), so the gap would fall inside the footprint. B-13 records bridges under lettering; the Living item says nothing about bridging.
Nothing ties a polyline to a settlement or to a mode (through or beside).
supplier.proposed_acceptance: For each of the 19 anchors in per_city with verdict printed-river (20 if the anchor-on-label fix lands and Stony Ford is added): the traced polyline crosses the 2.5*FOOT_R circle within 5 deg of every bearing listed here, crosses the 1.0*FOOT_R box edge at the listed perimeter bearings, and lies within 1 atlas px of river-ink inside the box (gaps under lettering bridged and listed); and for the anchors marked none, no traced vertex lies inside the box. Run the same check at the marker dots if anchors move.

hash.is_a_river_fix_hash_changing: Yes for the genCityCanvas source pin; no for cityCanvasSha if the change is RV-guarded. This corrects the brief's 'any fix changes cityCanvasSha'.
hash.atlas_fn_sha: tools/mobile-capture.js pins the source of each of: for (const n of ['xmur3', 'mulberry32', 'genCityCanvas', 'washMake', 'sampleCityMask']). Taking river geometry from atlas data means editing the RV block (var rvFa=...), so atlas_fn_sha.genCityCanvas changes on any such fix. docs/mobile/gates.md UG3: 'Atlas: the diff touches none of `xmur3`, `mulberry32`, `genCityCanvas`, `washMake` or `sampleCityMask`, and cityCanvasSha is equal to B0 and equal across all five profiles'. So a fix cannot land inside a Mobile atlas-lane unit; it queues after Mobile 9 (MR-A), as the Living trace already does.
hash.cityCanvasSha: tools/mobile-capture.js hashes only for (const n of ['Tamaron', 'Sokundo', 'Kanae']). None of the three has traits.river, and none has printed river ink in its box or approach circle (Tamaron's early flags were the AURA HOTH lettering). genCityCanvas's own comment says 'Every rng draw is RV-guarded → riverless cities stay byte-identical'. A fix that only engages when a city has traits.river or an atlas polyline crosses its box leaves cityCanvasSha equal to B0. It changes the plans of the 18 river cities (and of Kolens) by design.
hash.what_would_move_cityCanvasSha: A change to the mask path, e.g. fixing the label-halo-as-sea effect in buildCityMask (r-b<=54 on halo cream) or feeding rivers into sampleCityMask, changes the masks of harbour plans, and all three hashed cities are harbours (Tamaron harbor true, sea E distPx 2; Sokundo harbor true, WSW distPx 2; Kanae harbor true, E distPx 5). That moves cityCanvasSha, and for sampleCityMask also its atlas_fn_sha.

overlap.anchor_on_label: shift_sources anchor-on-label (anchors on label text or a neighbour, not the ring-dot) changes this table. Re-run at the maps_markers.json dots for the 37 anchors more than 5 px off: Aldrakhar (14.1 px off) goes from approach-only to box ink 261 (nearest river 5.0 px; bearings 195.0, 357.5); Iet Ford (27.7 px) to box ink 377 (1.1 px; 98.5, 107.0, 272.8); Bash Dargis (23.4 px) from graze to box ink 235 (5.0 px; 82.9, 258.5). Stony Ford (22.8 px off) has the '...daukhor R.' through its dot (box ink 49, 8.5 px; 7.9, 73.9) but nothing within reach of its anchor, so it is a river town that is invisible here.
